full_judgment: 3. The plaintiff case in short is that the plaintiff, Raju Nessa owned and possessed the suit land under Mouza-Payerakhali, P.S. Iswardi by way of registered deed No. 3403 dated 27-3-1961 and she is still enjoying the possession of the suit land by constructing a house with paying the rent and the RS Khatian has been correctly prepared in her name. In this backdrop on 10-3-1993 the defendant by showing a registered deed of gift informed to the plaintiff that she gifted the schedule (Ka) land to the defendant by the said registered deed of gift and then the plaintiff became astonished and thereafter, the plaintiff collected the certified copy of the said deed executed on 21-4-1990 through her relative and having read the deed she confirmed that the defendant created a forged deed in respect of schedule (Kha) land of the plaint. The plaintiff never executed the gift deed to the defendant and never handed over the possession of the suit land to the defendant. The plaintiff never went to the Iswardi Sub-Registry office for executing the disputed deed. It is also contended that when the plaintiff became ill in the first half of Baishak of 1397 BS then the defendant (daughter of the plaintiff) and her husband brought the plaintiff in the Iswardi Hospital by Rickshaw-van for treatment and kept her in front of a building and thereafter the husband of defendant-petitioner told the plaintiff that he brought a compounder of a famous doctor with him and to collect medicine it was needed her finger print on some stamp and white papers kept in the hands of the said compounder. The plaintiff on good faith put her thump impression on those papers. Thereafter, the Doctor of that compounder came to the house of the plaintiff to see her while the doctor informed her that his compounder did not ask for any finger print or signature. The defendant and her husband in this way manipulated the forged deed of gift and hence, the suit.
